name: README.md
html:
Animations

Every animation system in luiskr.com V3 — what moves, who computes it, and where the math lives. The physics-heavy sims (orbits, differential rotation, solar wind, pulsation, climate cycles, fly-to easing) have their own deep-dive folder: physics-simulations/.

Compute placement policy

Per-frame work never awaits. Every animation channel lands on exactly one executor, chosen by where the data lives:

flowchart TD Q["animation channel"] --> A{"per-frame, per-pixel/vertex?"} A -->|"yes"| G["GPU — WebGPU TSL nodes / GLSL shaders"] A -->|"no — batch math"| B{"heavy + parallelizable?"} B -->|"yes"| W["WASM worker pool — wasm-pool.ts"] B -->|"no"| C["JS on main thread — synchronous"] G -.->|"probe fails / energy-saver"| C W -.->|"no wasm / no worker"| C
  • GPU first on desktop: WebGPU node materials (three.js TSL) with a WebGL2/GLSL fallback, then a CSS/2D fallback when webglContext probing fails entirely (?debug=webGLMode:fallback forces this).
  • WASM workers for batch CPU: spiral-fills, layout, scroll math, image decode and media hashing dispatch through core/utils/wasm/wasm-pool.ts; every entry point carries a JS fallback so threads/WASM absence never breaks a frame.
  • JS on the main thread only for per-node transforms a GPU can't see (scene-graph pivots, DOM tweens) — all cheap O(bodies) math.

Star Field (experiments/star-field)

The whole scene is one animation loop — engine/frame.ts ticks camera, orbits, fx, LOD and registry spawns each frame. Full physics detail is in physics-simulations; the channel inventory:

Channel Executor Source
Orbital motion JS scene graph frame.ts — conic r(θ) per body
Orbital inclination JS (static tilt) def.inc on each pivot
Axial spin + inertial lock JS scene graph spinner node counter-rotates pivot Y
Differential rotation JS/GPU galaxy rotor in frame/updates.ts
Nebula drift + breathing GPU sprite rotation frame/fx.ts — node.nebula layers
Solar-wind swell JS → uniforms SF_SOLAR_WIND activity cycle
Meteor impact flashes JS pooled sprites SF_METEOR pool in fx.ts
Stellar pulsation JS scale/glow def.pulse — radius oscillation
Climate cycle JS → material def.cycle slow albedo/ice modulation
Weather bands GPU rotation offset def.weather cloud-layer drift
Aurora ribbons GPU shimmer def.aurora polar glow layer
Corona + flares GPU sprite pulses def.flares/corona seeded bursts
Camera fly-to JS cubic tween engine/fly.ts — easeInOutCubic
Registry body spawn/evict JS + worker fills registry-body.ts LRU cache
Spiral-arm fills WASM worker engine/fill-worker.ts batch dispatch
Skybox / 139k star cloud GPU static points star-cloud.ts single draw call
sequenceDiagram participant R as rAF loop participant F as frame.ts participant U as updates.ts participant X as fx.ts participant C as camera.ts R->>F: tick(dt) F->>C: damping + fly-to tween F->>U: orbits — r=a(1-e²)/(1+e·cosθ) F->>U: axis locks, LOD, registry spawns F->>X: nebula layers, wind, meteors, X->>X: pulse, climate, weather, aurora F->>R: renderer.render(scene, camera)

Earth Playground (experiments/earth-playground)

A WebGPU Earth + space backdrop driven by earth/runtime/frame.ts:

  • Planetary spin — Earth mesh rotation.y advances by sidereal-rate dt each frame; the cloud shell counter-rotates at a slower differential so weather visibly shears past the surface.
  • Day/night terminator — a shader uniform tracks the sun direction; the surface material blends day/night textures across a soft scattering limb — pure GPU, zero CPU per pixel.
  • Atmosphere shells — fresnel-rim fresnel shells pulse with camera altitude so the blue halo swells as you approach.
  • Space backdrop parallax — space/ layers drift on pointer/scroll input for depth without a second render pass.

Website UI (website/)

DOM/component animations — all CSS-transform driven (compositor thread), honors prefers-reduced-motion:

  • Genie dialog (core/utils/motion/genie.ts) — modal scales out of the control that opened it via --genie-x/--genie-y transform-origin; zooms back in on close.
  • DrawText (components/media/draw-text/) — SVG stroke-dash handwriting reveal; segment timing is computed off-thread through the wasm-pool text-timing batch, then played as CSS transitions.
  • Scroll state (core/utils/motion/scroll-state.ts) — parallax / reveal progress is sampled once per frame and written to CSS custom properties; heavy easing math goes through wasm-scroll.ts.
  • Skeletons — shimmering --skel-bg-* gradient sweeps while real content streams in; pure CSS.
  • Carousel / mosaics — layout springs computed by wasm-layout.ts batches, applied as transforms.

CMS (cms/)

Editor micro-animations — section accordions, drag-reorder ghosts, toast slides — all CSS transform/opacity, token-timed via ANIMATION_DURATIONS; nothing animates layout properties.
